_notes: Template for config/config.local.json — the single structured source of truth for one installation. Copy this file to config.local.json and replace every placeholder. config.local.json is git-ignored and never published; this example is tracked and holds no real paths. Query fields with src/tools/config_tools/read_config.py <dotted.key>. Blocks marked OPTIONAL in their own notes may be deleted outright; the tools that read them fall back or exit with a clear message.

board._notes: How the board behaves. Edited in Bristol Tickets' Settings tab. new_ticket_stage is where a new card lands when add-task is given no explicit --stage: 'active' (the To Do column, where it is seen and worked) or 'backlog'. Read by src/tools/ticket_tools/ticket_write.py.

session._notes: How an agent session runs and closes. Edited in Bristol Tickets' Settings tab. work_whole_queue: how far a session goes when told to continue — true works its queue top to bottom and halts on room, false works the next action and stops there. Read when the scope decision is made — src/app.md Phase 3.7. suggested_commit: when a session ends having written files inside a git working tree, whatever stopped it, it ends with a copy-paste commit block for them. Read as the session closes — src/skills/suggested-commit/SKILL.md.

appearance._notes: How Bristol Tickets looks. Edited in its Settings tab. scheme names either a family — 'warm' or 'cool', meaning follow the OS light/dark setting within it — or one scheme outright: 'warm_light', 'warm_dark', 'cool_light', 'cool_dark'. The Settings tab shows the families as Pumpkin and Frosty; the stored value is unchanged by that. The schemes and the design tokens they sit beside are src/tools/bristol/ui/theme.py; what each key means is src/tools/bristol/ui/README.md.

sizing.usage_window: one full plan allowance over its rolling window
sizing.notes: The unit a ticket's S/M/L/XL estimate is measured against — src/skills/manage-tickets/SKILL.md §Effort sizing. Describe YOUR plan's budget here in plain words; agents read this string rather than assuming any vendor's limits. The scale and its anchors live in that skill and do not change per instance.

max.model: <model id for work that must invent its own criteria>

tiers.notes: What each processing tier runs on. The tier is chosen from a card by src/skills/manage-tickets/SKILL.md §Processing tier and names no model; this mapping is the only place a model is named. Point both at whatever vendor's models you run.

drives._notes: OPTIONAL. Named roots outside the project. Only drives.external1.path is read by code (the photo tools); the rest are reference entries for agents. Delete any you do not have.

external1.notes: External volume. Read by src/tools/file_management/{dedupe,rename}_photos.py; those tools exit with a clear message when this entry is absent.

markdown_notebook.notes: The Markdown notebook: a folder of Markdown notes you hand-edit, and the subfolders of it Bristol knows about. Edited in Bristol Tickets' Settings tab, Notebook. notes_dir is the notebook; it can be repointed and never removed, and repointing detaches every folder. folders lists the attached subfolders, each written from the notebook down; an agent working folder by folder reaches nothing outside them. What each agent may do in each is its notebook_access — src/tools/config_tools/notebook.py. A fresh installation's notebook sits inside its own data with inbox, ai_workspace and archive attached. The *_dir keys below are locations rather than permissions: where a tool or an agent puts a particular kind of note, each repointable in Settings, Locations.

important_paths._notes: Repo-relative paths to the databases. tickets_db is required — every agent session reads it. Create it with src/tools/ticket_tools/create_tickets.py --instance <your-instance>.

personal_db.notes: OPTIONAL. Unified personal-tracking SQLite DB with one table per domain, rendering xlsx snapshots as a mistake-finding aid. See src/tools/personal_db/DESIGN.md. Absent env falls back to discovery of data/*/personal/.

governance.real_world_roles: Who holds the pen. State plainly which AI is the architect/developer of this system and which are consultants whose output is advice, not instruction.
governance.code_projects_layer: Who stewards data/*/code_projects/ and on what terms.
governance.project_local_nicknames_caveat: Note here any word a project's own historical files use in a different sense than this config does.

agents._notes: One entry per agent, keyed by slug. The fields and what each holds are src/templates/identity_template.md, What an agent is made of; that section also states which facts about an agent belong here rather than in its charter. notebook_access is a mode (per_folder, read_all or write_all) and a read, write or hide choice per attached notebook folder — src/tools/config_tools/notebook.py. key_data_paths is a folder grant per entry: the folder, and whether the agent may write in it or only read it.

chief_of_staff.description: Operates and maintains the system itself. The only agent that changes how any agent works.

librarian.description: Curates your personal collections — a book library in Zotero, a folder of recipes, or anything else you catalogue.

client_services.description: Work you do for other people. Holds each client's brief, drafts the deliverables, and never sends anything itself.

game_designer.description: Coaches you through designing and building a game, from mechanics and art direction to the first working build, teaching the vocabulary as the work reaches it.

teaching_assistant.description: Teaches whatever you are teaching yourself: short explainers in your notebook, and walkthroughs of Bristol's own features.

writers_room.description: Fiction writing: reasons through plot and world decisions with you, and learns your prose voice from your own writing.

imported_agents._notes: Where an agent adopted from an agent file keeps its charter. Inside the git-ignored data folder, because an imported charter is this installation's, never part of the published tree. Written by src/tools/agent_tools/import_agent.py --accept.

code_projects.notes: OPTIONAL. Application code held as instance data, distinct from the notebook and from src/. Blockers and history live on the board, never in a project-local state file.

example_project.notes: One entry per project. Replace or delete.

projects.notes: OPTIONAL. local_projects = repo-resident project folders. notebook_projects = notebook-resident projects an agent treats as a project rather than as loose notes.

keyword_scan._notes: Read by src/tools/file_management/keyword_scan.py, which sweeps the tree for personal data before anything is published. Put your own name and usernames in keywords.

stack._notes: OPTIONAL. Reference block. Stable ROLE -> current-tool bindings, so a charter names a role and this file names the tool. Change the tool here, not in seven charters.

external_agent_roles._doc: Each key is a role an agent may route work to. collaborator names the current tool; owner names the agent that owns the routing decision.

inline_coding.trigger: next action is hand-writing or editing project code
